passage:
I'm Deepak. In Class 6 science, Elizabeth ma'am was explaining rainbows and I asked, "But why are the colours always in the same order?" She sighed. "Don't ask silly questions, Deepak. Stick to the book." A few people laughed. My face went hot.
After that I kept my hand down. I still wondered about things, like why ink spreads in water and why the moon has days, but I wrote them in the back of my notebook instead. I stopped asking anyone. Sometimes, when I see a rainbow, the question comes back and sits with me.

qa.q: What did Deepak ask about rainbows?
qa.a: Deepak asked why the colours are always in the same order.

qa.q: What did Deepak feel when Elizabeth ma'am said not to ask silly questions?
qa.a: Deepak felt embarrassed and ashamed, with a hot face, and stopped raising a hand.

qa.q: What could a teacher do so that a student like Deepak keeps asking?
qa.a: A teacher could welcome the question, or say it is a good one and give a moment for it later. A question box could also give a safe place.

qa.q: How might the classmates who laughed have seen the moment?
qa.a: They may have followed the teacher's tone and thought the question was silly, without realising how it landed on Deepak.

grounding: A child told not to ask silly questions stops asking, though the curiosity persists privately.

passage:
Note by Bhupen, class teacher, Class 5.
Binita used to ask a question in every lesson. A month ago another teacher told her in front of the class, "Don't ask silly questions." Since then she has not raised her hand once, though she still studies the wall charts and scribbles on the last page of her notebook.
I have put a question box on my desk. Yesterday I found a folded slip: "Why do stars look small but are big?" I answered it aloud without naming anyone. This morning Binita lifted her hand for the first time in weeks. I will keep the box open, and I will keep answering.
— Bhupen

qa.q: Where did Bhupen put the question box?
qa.a: Bhupen put the question box on the desk.

qa.q: What did Binita probably feel when told not to ask silly questions in front of the class?
qa.a: Binita likely felt embarrassed and discouraged, and stopped raising her hand, while the curiosity carried on privately.

qa.q: What did Bhupen do that made it safe for Binita to ask again?
qa.a: Bhupen offered a question box, answered a slip aloud without naming anyone, and kept it open. That let Binita ask without being exposed.

qa.q: How does Bhupen read Binita's silence?
qa.a: Bhupen sees it as curiosity dampened, not gone, since Binita still studies the charts and writes in the notebook.

grounding: A child who is told not to ask silly questions stops asking; a teacher creates a safe way to bring the questions back.
